text.aura: The aura you carry is a garden in late spring: warm, welcoming and quietly abundant. Gi has a nurturing, soft-focus presence that makes people feel at home within minutes. You read as kind, thoughtful and genuinely interested, the person who notices someone standing alone at a party and goes over. Your glow is generous and practical, the comfort of good food and a well-lit kitchen. People feel better after spending time with you, even if they can't explain why. The glow-up for you isn't becoming more striking or dramatic. It's letting your own needs and taste take up as much room as your care for others. When you tend to yourself as well as you tend to everyone else, the whole garden blooms.
text.how-people-read-you: What people see first: friendly, approachable, a bit modest. People assume you're the reliable one, the friend who'll remember birthdays, and they're right. You rarely come across as intimidating, which means people open up to you fast. The misreading: they might think you don't have strong opinions, or that you're happy to go along with anything. In reality, you have very clear ideas, you just rarely push them. You can also be read as less ambitious than you are, because you don't advertise your goals. To be read more accurately, speak about what you want, not just what others need. Wear something with a bit of personality. Let your humor come out early. Gentle and powerful are not opposites. You're both.
text.colors: The colors that feel like home on you are soft Earth: oatmeal, cream, honey, butter yellow, warm taupe, caramel. These feel natural and comforting on you, like freshly baked bread in color form. Fire nourishes Earth, so soft warm tones like peach, apricot and dusty rose add a lovely glow, especially near your face. Muted greens like sage and olive feel garden-fresh against your neutrals. For jewelry, warm gold, pearls and soft ceramic or wooden pieces suit your energy. Avoid too much cold, stark color, like icy gray or harsh black and white contrast, which can make your warm presence read flat. Your best palette looks like a sunlit kitchen with flowers on the table.
text.style: Your look is cozy refined. Soft knits, relaxed trousers, comfortable dresses, cardigans with good buttons, a great tote bag that holds everything. You look your best when you look comfortable and cared for at the same time. Natural fabrics like cotton, linen and wool suit you. The trap is dressing purely for function: whatever's easy, whatever's clean, whatever keeps you invisible so the attention stays on others. Try building a few "you" pieces into your rotation, a printed blouse, a beautiful scarf, earrings that make you smile. Hair soft and touchable, makeup fresh and warm. Your best photo is at a café table or at a picnic, holding something you made or chose, smiling at the person behind the camera.
text.vibe: Your glow-up looks like the nurturer who also takes up space. Think of the comforting best friend in a K-drama who finally gets her own storyline and turns out to be the most interesting character. The shift for you is self-priority. Name your own preference, even when the easy option is right there. Take compliments without immediately deflecting. Spend money on something just for you, not useful, just lovely. Book the plan you've been suggesting for months and invite people to join you. Your warmth is magnetic. When you add confidence and a clear sense of your own taste, people start seeing you not just as the kind one, but as someone they genuinely want to impress.
text.aura-dims: Your light drops when you're over-giving. You look tired, scattered and a little overlooked. Your style slides into whatever's clean, your voice gets quieter in group conversations, and your worries start showing on your face as a permanent slight frown. You're tending everyone else's garden and letting yours grow weeds. The reset is gentle self-care that's actually about you. Cook a meal only you love. Spend an afternoon alone without errands. Buy yourself flowers, wear the soft color that makes you feel pretty, write down three things you want this month. Hand one responsibility back to someone else. A garden doesn't bloom by giving all its soil away. Keep some for yourself.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, your aura is a garden. People feel at home with you in five minutes.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Because you've already fed them, found them a charger and asked about their mom.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Honey, cream, peach and sage. You look like a sunny kitchen.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You dress like you're trying not to be noticed. Why?

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your glow-up is taking up space. Your taste deserves the spotlight too.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Take the compliment. Don't say "oh this old thing." Just say thank you.

spring.intro: With spring Wood drawing on the soil, a spring Gi aura is a garden bed in April: busy, generous and full of other people's seedlings. Most people see you as kind, approachable and helpful, the friend who always has a spare charger and a pen. Your style can vanish into usefulness: soft neutrals, practical bags, nothing that asks for attention. Your glow-up is warmth with intention. Fire feeds Earth, so peach, clay, coral and warm rose bring life to your palette. Add one considered detail people will associate with you, a hand-thrown ceramic ring or a woven bag in a color you chose. The spring Gi glow is a garden in morning sun, inviting and unmistakably tended.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Gi, you carry everyone's charger. Carry a coral bag too. One that's only for you.

summer.intro: Summer Fire feeds Earth, so a summer Gi aura is warm, fertile soil, and people read you as nurturing, grounded and confident in your taste. You likely look great in warm earthy tones and know it. The trap is heaviness. With strong support, your look can feel overcomplete: layered necklaces, a bag full of everything, three warm neutrals that blur into one. Your glow-up is lightness. Metal, the element Earth produces, brings white, silver and clean shapes, while a touch of Water blue keeps the heat fresh. Swap one layer for one crisp piece and see how much easier you look. The summer Gi glow is a sunlit courtyard: warm, tidy and calm.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Gi, take off one necklace and add a white shirt. You'll breathe like a courtyard.

autumn.intro: Autumn Metal draws on Earth to exist, so an autumn Gi aura is the field after harvest: generous, golden and a little worn out. Most people see you as capable and warm, the one who remembers everybody's coffee order and their dog's name. You give so much that your style can slide into whatever was clean this morning. Your glow-up is refilling the soil. Fire is your resource, so deep coral, rust, mustard and cinnamon put warmth back into your look, and a tactile accessory, a leather strap or a clay bead bracelet, keeps you grounded. Dress for your own day, not just for helping with everyone else's. The autumn Gi glow is golden-hour wheat.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Gi, 'whatever was clean' isn't a style. Mustard knit, clay beads. Dress for your day.

winter.intro: Born when Water rules, a Gi Earth spends its strength holding that Water in place, so a winter Gi aura is cold, quiet ground under frost: private, steady and full of hidden potential. You come across as calm and modest, sometimes so modest they forget to notice you. Your wardrobe likely leans gray, black and safe, the quietest coat on the rack. Your glow-up is warmth and visibility. Fire is what wintry soil craves, so bring in warm red, apricot, mustard and terracotta. Soft textures like brushed wool and velvet help your warmth feel touchable. Wear one color that makes strangers comment. A winter Gi in warm color is a greenhouse in January.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Gi, apricot velvet in January. People will want to step into your warmth.

earth.intro: Born when Earth takes over the end of a season, a Gi aura is rich garden soil: warm, nurturing and soft to be around. People feel looked after near you. You may dress for comfort and practicality first, and a lot of it lands in beige. With extra Earth in your chart, your glow-up is freshness. Metal draws Earth out, so silver, pearl and clean white brighten you, and fresh green reminds people that things grow around you. A tidy collar or a silver earring does a lot of work.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Gi, the oatmeal sweater is lovely. Add one silver thing so we can find you.

strength.strong: A strong Gi Earth aura is fertile soil with everything growing at once. With plenty of Earth and Fire, you come across as nurturing and capable, and your style can get cluttered: layers, scarves, two bags, a little of everything just in case someone needs it. The blind spot is overpowering through abundance. Simplify with Metal: one clean white top, one silver piece, fewer layers and a lighter bag. Keep your warmth in the palette, not the volume. People will see you more clearly when there is less to look at. A garden is lovelier with a path through it.
strength.weak: A weak Gi Earth aura is thin soil that gives everything away. With little Earth or Fire support, you dress for usefulness and comfort, and you rarely buy anything simply because you love it. The blind spot is over-giving: your money, time and attention go to everyone else while your wardrobe stays an afterthought. Your glow-up is one indulgence. A warm-toned knit, a beautiful ceramic ring, a bag in terracotta you would never call practical. Choose it purely because it delights you, and wear it often. Let your style say that you matter too.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood gives your aura lots of drive and upward energy, but it can read as restless or intense, always busy, always growing. Your style may lean practical and outdoorsy, sometimes at the expense of polish. Balance it with Metal touches: a crisp white shirt, silver jewelry, cleaner lines, one tailored piece. Declutter your wardrobe so what remains feels intentional. Your glow is strongest when your ambition looks calm, like a tall tree that doesn't need to prove it's growing.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means your aura can lack a sense of freshness and new beginnings. You might stick to the same outfits for years or feel unsure about trying new styles. Bring in Wood: greens, botanical prints, natural fabrics like linen and cotton, plants in your space. Try one new style element each month, a different silhouette, a new accessory, a new hair clip. Growth looks good on you. Let your style evolve a little, the way spring changes a garden.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your aura bright, bold and sometimes overwhelming. Whether you wear it loudly or quietly, your look can carry more heat than the moment needs: one statement too many, or an intensity people feel before you've said a word. Balance it with Water: navy, deep blue, black accents, calmer silhouettes. Choose one statement per outfit instead of five. Let some quiet into your presence too, listening more, moving slower. Your glow is already strong. Cooling it slightly makes it look richer and more confident.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means your aura can feel understated, sometimes so understated that people overlook you. You might default to neutrals and avoid anything that draws attention. Bring in Fire: a red lip, a coral scarf, warm gold jewelry, a little shimmer. Seek out sunlight in photos and in life. Let yourself be seen in small ways: post the photo, wear the bright thing, laugh openly. Visibility is a skill, and it looks lovely on you when you allow it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth gives you a grounded, warm aura that can slide into heavy or overly practical. Your wardrobe may be comfortable but samey, lots of beige, brown and safe basics. Balance it with Wood: fresh greens, lighter fabrics, a playful print, something that moves when you walk. Try one unexpected piece. Rearrange your space for a fresh feeling. Your stability is beautiful. A little lightness on top keeps it from looking stuck.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth can make your aura feel scattered or ungrounded, lots of ideas, many style moods, not much consistency. Your outfits may change wildly depending on your mood. Bring in Earth: camel, beige, warm brown, ochre, and solid basics like a good coat and reliable shoes. Build a small capsule wardrobe you can trust. Ceramics, wood and warm lighting at home help too. When your foundation is steady, your creativity looks intentional instead of chaotic.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives your aura sharpness and polish that can tip into cold or severe. Your style may be immaculate but a little untouchable: very clean lines, lots of black, white and gray, everything controlled. Balance it with Fire: warm colors near your face, soft textures, a smile that comes sooner. Let one thing be imperfect on purpose, rolled sleeves, tousled hair, a playful accessory. Precision is your strength. Warmth makes it inviting.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal can make your aura feel soft but a little undefined. People like you, but they might not remember your style clearly. Bring in Metal: silver jewelry, crisp white, sharp tailoring, clean shoes, a structured bag. Edit your wardrobe so every piece earns its place. A clear signature, the same ring, the same scent, a consistent color, gives your look definition. Clarity doesn't make you colder. It makes you memorable.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water gives your aura depth and mystery, but it can read as distant, moody or hard to reach. You might hide in dark colors and oversized layers. Balance it with Earth: warm neutrals near your face, structured pieces, a grounded silhouette. Add a little Fire too, a coral or rose accent, to bring warmth. Let people see your expression clearly. Your mystery is magnetic. A bit of warmth makes it feel welcoming, not unreachable.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means your aura can feel busy and bright without much depth or calm. You might always be on, always moving, with little stillness. Bring in Water: navy, midnight blue, black, flowing fabrics, a more relaxed silhouette. Create quiet moments in your day and let them show in your style, softer textures, fewer accessories. Water by your bed and slow evenings help your energy settle. Depth looks good on you. Give it some room.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: hiking boots, three plants and a tote bag. Add one sharp silver thing.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your freshness is gorgeous. A crisp white shirt makes it look intentional.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: red bag, gold chain, leopard coat. Pick one. The others can wait.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your warmth is your magic. Let navy or stone frame it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: beige, oatmeal, sand, more beige. You look like a very calm cupboard.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is beautiful. One silver piece or a deep blue lifts it.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: you look expensive and impossible to talk to. Add one soft texture.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your polish is stunning. A warm knit lets people come closer.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: all black, all mystery, all the time. Even vampires wear burgundy.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is magnetic. A warm color helps people find the door.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Try a sage scarf or a leafy print. Let your style grow a little.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Same outfit since 2021 isn't a signature. It's a rut with good lighting.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? A coral scarf or warm gold earrings changes how people greet you.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: Head-to-toe gray says 'don't notice me'. Is that really the message?

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? A camel coat or a terracotta bag grounds your whole look.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Five trends this month, zero signature. Commit to something longer than a week.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? A crisp white shirt or a silver cuff gives your look clean edges.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Everything slightly creased and slightly oversized reads accidental. Tailor one piece.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? Deep navy or a fluid silk adds calm depth to your look.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Always bright, always on. Let one outfit be quiet. People lean in.
